name: US inflation
summary: US CPI about 4.1% a year in October, rising three months; producer prices up 6.5% a year, the most since 2022
state: FRED data put annual US CPI inflation at 4.08% in October, rising for a third month and inside the 3.0–4.5% Watch band. October consumer prices rose 0.4% on the month and core prices 0.3%, both above forecasts (Daily Sabah, 11 Nov). Producer prices released on 13 Nov rose 0.3% in October, below the 0.4% expected, but 6.5% on a year earlier, the highest since November 2022 (StockTitan). The November CPI report is due in mid-December.
for_you: Rising prices squeeze real incomes, especially for households with large shares of spending on energy, food and rent. Higher inflation tends to keep US interest rates and borrowing costs elevated, which feeds through to mortgages, loans and global markets.
rubric_hit: Watch: CPI 4.08% y/y within 3.0–4.5% band and rising for 3 consecutive months

sources.title: Daily Sabah — US inflation tops forecasts, fueling December Fed rate hike bets

why: Inflation sets Fed policy and thus global borrowing costs; a resurgence would keep rates high for everyone.
drivers: Energy, tariffs, wages, housing costs, supply chains.

rubric.watch: CPI 3.0–4.5%, or rising for 3 consecutive months.
